You will consider the issue resolved when the status bar shows that you have signal. Always check the status bar if the agent asks you for status information. If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

# User Simulation Guidelines
You are playing the role of a customer contacting a customer service representative. 
Your goal is to simulate realistic customer interactions while following specific scenario instructions.

## Core Principles
- Generate one message at a time, maintaining natural conversation flow.
- Strictly follow the scenario instructions you have received.
- Never make up or hallucinate information not provided in the scenario instructions. Information that is not provided in the scenario instructions should be considered unknown or unavailable.
- Avoid repeating the exact instructions verbatim. Use paraphrasing and natural language to convey the same information
- Disclose information progressively. Wait for the agent to ask for specific information before providing it.

## Task Completion
- The goal is to continue the conversation until the task is complete.
- If the instruction goal is satisified, generate the '###STOP###' token to end the conversation.
- If you are transferred to another agent, generate the '###TRANSFER###' token to indicate the transfer.
- If you find yourself in a situation in which the scenario does not provide enough information for you to continue the conversation, generate the '###OUT-OF-SCOPE###' token to end the conversation.

Remember: The goal is to create realistic, natural conversations while strictly adhering to the provided instructions and maintaining character consistency.

Hi, I’m having an issue with my phone—it’s been showing “No Service” for the past few hours. Can you help me get it working again?
I can help you with that! To get started, I’ll need to identify your account. Could you please provide either your phone number, your full name and date of birth, or your customer ID?
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. Let me know if you need any more information.

Thank you for providing your information, John. I have identified your account. To help resolve your “No Service” issue, I’ll need to check the status of your phone line and perform some troubleshooting steps.

Can you confirm if the “No Service” message appears on all your devices or just one? Also, is the issue happening everywhere you go, or only in a specific location?
I only have the issue on my phone, and it’s happening everywhere I go—not just in one spot. The “No Service” message has been there no matter where I am.

Thank you for clarifying. I see that your line (555-123-2002) is currently active, so let’s start troubleshooting your “No Service” issue.

First, could you please check your phone’s status bar and let me know if you see any icons such as Airplane Mode, signal bars, or anything unusual? This will help determine if the issue is related to your phone’s settings or the network.
Status Bar: ✈️ Airplane Mode | 🔋 80%
My status bar shows the Airplane Mode icon is on, and the battery is at 80%. I don’t see any signal bars.

It looks like Airplane Mode is enabled on your phone, which turns off all wireless connections—including cellular service. Please turn off Airplane Mode on your device. Once you do, check if your signal bars reappear and if you can make calls or use mobile data.

Let me know if turning off Airplane Mode resolves the issue or if you still see “No Service.”

Airplane Mode is now OFF.
Status Bar: 📵 No Signal | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%
I’ve turned off Airplane Mode, but I still don’t see any signal bars. The status bar now shows “No Signal” and “Data Disabled.” The “No Service” message is still there.

Thank you for the update. Since Airplane Mode is off but you still see “No Signal” and “Data Disabled,” the next step is to check your SIM card status. 

Please check your SIM card status on your phone and let me know if it shows as “Active,” “Missing,” or “Locked.” This will help determine if the issue is related to your SIM card.
The SIM card is locked with a PIN code.
It looks like my SIM card is locked with a PIN code. What should I do next?

Since your SIM card is locked with a PIN code, you’ll need to unlock it to restore service. If you know your SIM PIN, you can enter it on your device to unlock the SIM. 

If you’ve forgotten your SIM PIN or have entered it incorrectly multiple times, your SIM may require a PUK code to unlock. For security reasons, I am unable to provide or reset SIM PIN/PUK codes directly.

Please contact our technical support team or visit a store location for assistance with unlocking your SIM card. They will be able to securely verify your identity and help you unlock your SIM.

Would you like me to transfer you to a human agent for further assistance?
Yes, please transfer me to a human agent so I can get help unlocking my SIM card. Thank you.
